title: Choose Tripwire's visual world
question: The roll assigned Ward Call Light: calm, pastel, and quiet until an agent trips. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Ward Call Light
options.lineage: Hospital ward corridors: celadon walls, nurse-call dome lights above each door
options.thesis: Nurses don't watch every room. A light comes on when someone needs them. Tripwire works the same way.
options.viewport: A left nav rail, then three agent lanes as ward rooms, each with a dome light at its head (off and frosted when calm, glowing coral on a trip), and a steady step feed under each.
options.risk: Pastel green can read as healthcare branding if the call light, the signature move, is set timidly.

raised.raise: Every lost star sits beside the exact event that proves it. No claim appears without its evidence.
The kill chain is drawn as one line with ordered stations (exposure, persistence, relay, execution), at disciplined right angles.
State is never carried by color alone: a solid line means live, dashed means paused, struck through means revoked.
Every trip and canary gets a stable short number (TRP-0007) that is used everywhere it appears.

options.label: Security Paper
options.lineage: Cheque and certificate security paper: guilloche, hidden marks that reveal tampering
options.thesis: Security paper hides marks that only show when someone tampers with it. That's a canary, printed.
options.viewport: A clean dashboard on a pale green security tint. Rating placards and the Trust Report carry a fine guilloche border; a tripped canary prints a red VOID mark across its card.
options.risk: Guilloche turns into decoration if used beyond the report and placards; it's the most 'certificate-like' and least calm of the three.

options.label: Claim + Proof Monochrome
options.lineage: Monochrome software marketing: neutral scale, one sparing accent
options.thesis: Almost no color; every assertion sits next to the screenshot or event that proves it.
options.viewport: A neutral dashboard, sentence-case headings, a sage accent used only for the primary action and live state, trips in a single muted red.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds product clarity, but loses on audience identification: it misses the 'feel safe' pastel you asked for.
options.risk: Can feel like every other SaaS dashboard; the calm comes from removing things, not from color.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Agent runs as colored lines; trips as interchanges.
options.viewport: Each agent a colored line across a midnight map.
options.case: The midnight ground fights your pastel, safe brief.
options.risk: Too dark and too loud for a calm product.
options.kept: Kill chain as one line with ordered stations at right angles.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one rail; state is line form.
options.viewport: A single rail of hairline marks.
options.case: Charcoal and single-size type cost clarity on a projector.
options.kept: State carried by line form (solid/dashed/struck), not color alone.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every artifact gets a catalog number.
options.viewport: Black field, one plot, a number.
options.case: Matte black is the opposite of 'safe and calm'.
options.kept: Stable short IDs (TRP-0007) for every trip and canary.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight and case.
options.viewport: Raked slides on a lit bed.
options.case: Raked containers and goldenrod hurt clarity and calm.
options.kept: A tight type scale: rank by weight before size.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean security SaaS dashboard: white, slate, one blue accent, sidebar nav.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, a KPI row, a table of agents, a trips table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other security dashboard by design.
